rows.visual_alignment: Caption #1 says Brahma chose to test Krishna and hid calves. The source image is Brahma riding a swan; it is a thematic portrait, not a depiction of the concealment. Scene plan follows the Sanskrit decision to test and hide the calves.
rows.caption_vs_canonical_sanskrit: Caption #1 connects the Aghasura episode to Brahma’s test and hiding the calves; both the prior Aghasura deliverance and the test are present in stanza 52-1.

rows.visual_alignment: Caption #2 tracks the search and concealment; the source image shows Brahma above cowherd boys in a cave but omits Krishna and the calves. It illustrates only part of the caption and broader story.
rows.caption_vs_canonical_sanskrit: The search, Krishna’s half-eaten meal and Brahma hiding the boys align with stanza 52-2; the cave detail is a traditional narrative expansion not stated in this verse.

rows.visual_alignment: Caption #3 is an accurate summary of multiplication and return. The source image is a glossy multi-form devotional assembly, without a clearly readable group of calves or evening return; keep it as context, not a composition template.
rows.caption_vs_canonical_sanskrit: Krishna becoming the calves and cowherd boys and returning to Vraja in the evening align with stanza 52-3.

rows.visual_alignment: The source image shows cowherd boys and calves welcomed by women and cows, matching the caption and verse.
rows.caption_vs_canonical_sanskrit: The cowherd women and cows receiving the returned boys and calves joyfully aligns with stanza 52-4.

rows.visual_alignment: The source image depicts mothers and cows embracing child-like forms; it supports the caption’s affection theme but does not show the verse’s metaphysical distinction in literal terms.
rows.caption_vs_canonical_sanskrit: The women and cows rejoicing on receiving Krishna as their own child aligns with stanza 52-5; the caption’s general statement about parenthood is commentary.

rows.visual_alignment: The caption’s year-end realization by Balarama is canonical. The source image shows a general reunion with children, mothers and cattle; Balarama’s realization is not visually explicit.
rows.caption_vs_canonical_sanskrit: Balarama recognizing the difference at year’s end aligns with stanza 52-6; the phrase “both are brahma swaroopam” is interpretive commentary.

rows.visual_alignment: The image is a broad devotional rendering of four-armed divine forms and a pastoral gathering; Brahma’s year-end recognition is not clearly distinguished. Canonical text controls the planned scene.
rows.caption_vs_canonical_sanskrit: Brahma seeing the new and old calfherds as four-armed, cloud-hued forms aligns with stanza 52-7.

rows.visual_alignment: The source image directly shows reclining Narayana, Lakshmi at his feet and Brahma on a lotus. The group of sages in the caption and verse is not clearly shown.
rows.caption_vs_canonical_sanskrit: The Narayana vision with Lakshmi, serpent couch and sages aligns with stanza 52-8.

rows.visual_alignment: The caption describes Brahma’s bewilderment and the single Krishna with half-eaten food. The source image reads as a pastoral meal with multiple child forms; Brahma and the dissolving Narayana forms are not clearly legible.
rows.caption_vs_canonical_sanskrit: Brahma’s bewilderment before innumerable Narayana forms and their resolution into one Krishna holding half-eaten food aligns with stanza 52-9.

rows.visual_alignment: The source image depicts Brahma bowing to Krishna, matching the opening action in the caption. It omits the restored boys and calves and their joyful homecoming; the planned scene follows the complete canonical stanza.
rows.caption_vs_canonical_sanskrit: Brahma’s praise and departure, Krishna’s joyful entry home with boys and calves, and the appeal for relief from illness align with stanza 52-10.
